 N12/P1 INTERVENORS’ REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS TO PROPOSAL FOR DECISION
TO THE TEXAS PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION:

KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P.; Quillen Family Partnership, Ltd.; William Quillen; James Blake
Quillen; Carolyn Quillen; and Pfluger Family Limited Partnership (collectively, the “N12/PI
Intervenors”), respectfully submit this Reply to Exceptions to Proposal for Decision.

I. Introduction

KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P.; Quillen Family Partnership, Ltd.; William Quillen; James Blake
Quillen; Carolyn Quillen; and Pfluger Family Limited Partnership all own property on Link N12
and Link P1. KLM Griffin Ranch, L.P. also owns property on Link O1. The N12/P1 Intervenors
support Route 894, Route 487, and other routes that do not utilize Links N12, O1 and/or P1.

This proceeding involves Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC’s (“Oncor”) and the
LCRA Transmission Service Corporation’s (‘LCRA”) (Oncor and LCRA are collectively referred
to as “Applicants” herein) joint application to amend their certificate of convenience and necessity
for the Bell County East Switch to the Big Hill Substation 765kV transmission line project.
Applicants proposed Route 894 as the route that “best meets” the statutory routing criteria and that
conforms with the Public Utility Commission’s (the “Commission’’) policies. The Public Utility
Commission Staff (the “PUC Staff’), recommends Route 487 as the “best meets” route. The
Commission must select a route that “consider[s] the totality of all factors, even if individual
factors—considered in isolation—could lead to opposite outcomes,” and “[n]Jone of the statutory
factors is intended to be absolute in the sense that any one shall prevail in all possible

circumstances.”

D. Hearing on the Merits

As noted previously, the Hearing on the Merits was conducted in Austin over five (5) days
in the period from June 8 to June 12, 2026. Despite the large number of parties in the case,
appearing both in person and virtually, the hearing was compressed into a five-day window with
daily beginning and ending times rigorously enforced. This resulted in parties being limited in
their cross examination of witnesses. The Brady Creek Intervenors complain that the limited cross
examination deprived them of their right to due process and impeded their ability to develop their
case.> While this may be true, ALL parties were faced with the exact same time constraints. Like
the Brady Creek Intervenors, the N12/P1 Intervenors would have liked more time to develop their
case. However, ALL parties were faced with the same time constraints, and ALL parties were
forced to play by the same rules. The Brady Creek Intervenors also complain that they had aligned
clients with different issues in the case and that forcing them into one block of shared time was
unfair.© However, the N12/P1 Intervenors also consist of clients with disparate issues and were
similarly allocated one block of shared time, as was each other group of aligned intervenors. Thus,

the time allotments were fair. The Brady Creek Intervenors do not show that with additional time,

The N12/P1 Intervenors support Routes 894 and 487, as well as any other routes that do
not utilize Links N12, Ol, or P1. The Exceptions filed by various parties do not alter the record
evidence demonstrating that when ALL applicable routing factors are applied, Routes 894 and 487
provide more reasonable and balanced routing choices than Routes 392, 410, 894 (Western Mod
1), and any other routes utilizing Links N12, O1, or P1. Although no single route performs best

under every routing criterion, the Commission must consider the routing criteria as a whole rather

i. Route 894 (Central Corridor)

The N12/P1 Intervenors support the ALJs’ routing recommendation of Route 894.8 Route
894 is approximately 223.17 miles long, has an estimated transmission-line cost of

approximately 98.02 miles of existing compatible rights-of-way.? The Exceptions criticizing Route
894 largely focus on localized impacts to particular properties. While those impacts should be
considered, they must be weighed against the impacts that alternative routes would impose on
other landowners and against the remaining statutory criteria. No route eliminates landowner

area.

number of parties opposed to Route 392 was the late addition of several links, which likely
